core_obligations: Choose generators of the algebra and monic polynomials annihilating them (proof lines 4596-4598).
Apply the adjoining-a-root lemma once per linear factor to obtain a finite free extension where the polynomials split completely (proof lines 4599-4605).
Map the polynomial ring onto the base changed algebra and check the chosen polynomials die (proof lines 4606-4611).
proof_roadmap: Generators and their monic polynomials (proof lines 4596-4598).
Split the polynomials after a finite free extension (proof lines 4599-4605).
Present the algebra as a quotient (proof lines 4606-4611).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that after a finite free ring extension, a finite algebra becomes a quotient of a polynomial ring by monic polynomials that split completely into linear factors. The proof chooses generators of the algebra over the ring, picks a monic polynomial for each generator annihilating it, and then applies the adjoining-a-root lemma once for each linear factor required, which produces a finite free extension in which all the polynomials split. Mapping the variables to the generators realises the algebra as a quotient of the polynomial ring modulo the now split polynomials.
